x: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Commentary on the sura "al-Taghābun" (Mutual Loss and Gain).
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h
Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies God. To Him belongs dominion, and to Him belongs praise, and He is over all things competent (1)
The Exalted says: whatever is in the seven heavens and whatever is on the earth of His creation prostrates to Him and magnifies Him.
His saying:
h
To Him belongs dominion
. The Exalted says: to Him belong the dominion of the heavens and the earth and their sovereignty
n
; His decree concerning all of that is carried out, and His command is effective in it.
His saying:
h
and to Him belongs praise

. He says: and to Him belongs the praise of every created thing in them; for all of the creation in them know good only from Him, and they have no provider besides Him, so to Him belongs the praise of all of them.
h
And He is over all things competent

. He says: He is over everything possessed of power. He says: He creates what He wills and causes to die whom He wills, enriches whom He wills and impoverishes whom He wills, exalts whom He wills and abases whom He wills; nothing He wills is beyond Him, because He possesses perfect power, which nothing can overcome.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h
It is He who created you, and among you is the disbeliever and among you is the believer; and God, of what you do, is Seeing (2)
The Exalted says: God is
h
He who created you
, O people — and this is a mention of the name of God —
h
and among you is the disbeliever and among you is the believer
. He says: [among you is a disbeliever in his Creator and in the fact that He created him,
h
and among you is a believer
. He says]
n
: among you is one who believes in Him and is certain that He is his Creator and Maker,
h
and God, of what you do, is Seeing

. He says: and God, who created you, is Seeing of your deeds, knowing them, none of them hidden from Him, and He will repay you for them, so fear Him lest you oppose Him in His command or His prohibition, so that He falls upon you.

c: Muḥammad b. Manṣūr al-Ṭūsī told us, he said:
m: told us, he said: Ibn Lahīʿa told us, he said: Bakr b. Sawāda told us, from Abū Tamīm al-Jayshānī

, from Abū Dharr, he said: When the semen has remained in the womb forty nights, the angel of the souls comes and ascends with it to the Almighty in his palm, and says: O Lord, this servant of yours, male or female? And God decrees concerning it what He decrees. Then he says: O Lord, wretched or fortunate? And He writes what he will meet. He said: And Abū Dharr recited the opening of "al-Taghābun", five verses

x: Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h
He created the heavens and earth in truth and formed you and perfected your forms; and to Him is the destination (3)
The Exalted says: He created the seven heavens (*) and the earth with justice and fairness,
h
and formed you
. He says: and fashioned you and made your fashioning good. It is said: What is meant by that is His forming of Adam and His creating him with His hand.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muḥammad b. Saʿd told me, he said: My father related to me, he said: My uncle related to me, he said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās:
m: He created the heavens and earth in truth and formed you and perfected your forms
. He said: He means Adam; He created him with His hand.

x: His saying:
h
and to Him is the destination
. He says: and to God is the return of all of you, O people.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Mighty and Majestic:
h
He knows what is in the heavens and earth and knows what you conceal and what you declare; and God is Knowing of that within the breasts (4)

Abū Jaʿfar (may God have mercy on him) said: The Exalted says: your Lord, O people, knows whatever is in the seven heavens and the earth; nothing hidden of it is concealed from Him; and He knows what you conceal, O people, [within yourselves]
n
, of word and deed, and what you declare of it and so make manifest;
h
and God is Knowing of that within the breasts

. Mighty is His praise says: God has knowledge of the inner thoughts in the breasts of His servants and of what their souls enfold, which is more hidden than a secret; nothing of that escapes Him. The Exalted says to His servants: beware of concealing other than what you declare, or of keeping in yourselves other than what you show, for your Lord is not hidden from anything of that; He counts all of it and watches over all of it for you.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Mighty and Majestic:
h

Has there not come to you the news of those who disbelieved before? So they tasted the bad consequence of their affair, and they will have a painful punishment (5) That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, but they said, "Shall human beings guide us?" and disbelieved and turned away, and God was not in need; and God is Free of need and Praiseworthy (6)

Abū Jaʿfar (may God have mercy on him) said: The Exalted says to the polytheists of Quraysh: Has there not come to you, O people, the report of those who disbelieved before you — such as the people of Noah, ʿĀd, Thamūd, the people of Abraham and the people of Lot —
h
so they tasted the bad consequence of their affair
: God's punishment touched them for their disbelief,
h
and they will have a painful punishment

. He says: and they will have an agonizing punishment on the Day of Resurrection in the fire of Hell, in addition to that with which God made them taste in this world the bad consequence of their disbelief.
His saying:
h
That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs
. Mighty is His praise says: this which befell
n

those who disbelieved before (*) these polytheists, of the bad consequence of their disbelief, and what their Lord has prepared for them on the Day of Resurrection of punishment — [is] because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs: those whom their Lord sent to them with evident evidences and signs of the truth of what they called them to; and they said to them:
h
Shall human beings guide us?

! — out of arrogance that God's messengers to them were human beings like themselves, and out of arrogance against following the truth because a human being like them had called them to it. He gathered the report about the human being, and said:
h
yahdūnanā
(they guide us) and did not say: yahdīnā (he guides us), because bashar, although in the form of a singular, has the sense of a plural.
His saying:
h
so they disbelieved and turned away
. He says: so they disbelieved in God and denied the message of His messengers whom God had sent to them, out of arrogance;
h
and turned away
. He says: they turned their backs on the truth and did not accept it, and they paid no heed to what their messengers called them to;
h
and God was not in need
. He says: God was free of need of them and of their faith in Him and in His messengers, and had no need of that from them;
h
and God is Free of need and Praiseworthy
. He says: God is free of need of all His creation, and praised by all of them for the beauty of His favors to them and the generosity of His acts toward them.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h

Those who disbelieved have claimed that they will never be resurrected. Say, "Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected; then you will surely be informed of what you did. And that, for God, is easy" (7)
The Exalted says:
h
claimed
— those who disbelieved in God — that God will never raise them up to Him from their graves after their death. Ibn ʿUmar used to say:
h
zaʿama
is the surname of lying.

c: Muḥammad b. Nāfiʿ al-Baṣrī told me that, he said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Mahdī told us, from Sufyān, from some of his companions,

x: His saying:
h
Say, "Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected"
. He says to His Prophet Muḥammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say to them, O Muḥammad: Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be raised from your graves,
h
then you will surely be informed of what you did
. He says: then you will surely be told of your deeds that you did in the world,
h
and that, for God, is easy
. He says: and your being raised from your graves after your death is easy and light for God.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h
So believe in God and His Messenger and the light which We have sent down; and God is Aware of what you do (8)

The Exalted says: so believe in God and His Messenger, O polytheists who deny the resurrection, and in His report to you that you will be raised after your death and that after your decay you will be brought forth from your graves,
h
and the light which We have sent down
. He says: and believe in the light that We have sent down, which is this Qur'an that God sent down upon His Prophet Muḥammad, may God bless him and grant him peace,
h
and God is Aware of what you do
. The Exalted says: and God, O people, is Aware of your deeds, encompassing them, counting all of them; none of them is hidden from Him, and He will repay you for all of them.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h

The Day He will gather you for the Day of Assembly — that is the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain. And whoever believes in God and does righteousness — He will remove from him his misdeeds and admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the great attainment (9)
The Exalted says: and God is Aware of what you do,
h
the Day He will gather you for the Day of Assembly
: for the day on which the creatures are gathered for the reckoning;
h
that is the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain
. He says: the assembly is the day of the people of Paradise's gain over the people of the Fire.
The interpreters said something like what we have said on this.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us; and al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Waraqāʾ told us,
m: both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid regarding God's saying:
that is the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain
. He said: It is the gain of the people of Paradise over the people of the Fire

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda:
m: The Day He will gather you for the Day of Assembly
: it is the Day of Resurrection, and it is the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain, the day of the gain of the people of Paradise over the people of the Fire

c: ʿAlī told me, he said: Abū Ṣāliḥ told us, he said: Muʿāwiya related to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās
m: that is the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain
: it is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection; He magnified it and warned His servants of it

x: His saying:
h
And whoever believes in God and does righteousness
. The Exalted says: whoever believes in God, acts in obedience to Him, and stops at His command and prohibition,
h
He will remove from him his misdeeds
. He says: He will wipe away his sins from him,
h
and admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow
. He says: and He will admit him to gardens beneath whose trees rivers flow.
His saying:
h
abiding therein forever
. He says: remaining in them forever; they will not die and will not leave them.
His saying:
h
That is the great attainment
. He says: their abiding in the gardens we have described is the great deliverance.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h
But those who disbelieved and denied Our signs — those are the companions of the Fire, abiding therein; and wretched is the destination (10)

The Exalted says: those who denied the oneness of God and rejected His evidences, His proofs and the verses of His Book which He sent down upon His servant Muḥammad, may God bless him and grant him peace,
h
those are the companions of the Fire, abiding therein
. He says: remaining in it forever; they will not die in it and will not leave it,
h
and wretched is the destination
. He says: and wretched is the thing to which one is brought: Hell.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h
No disaster strikes except by permission of God. And whoever believes in God — He will guide his heart; and God is Knowing of all things (11)
The Exalted says: no disaster has struck anyone of the creation
h
except by permission of God
. He says: except by God's decree and His having ordained that for him;
h
and whoever believes in God — He will guide his heart
. He says: whoever believes in God and so knows that no one is struck by a disaster except by God's permission for it,
h
He will guide his heart
. He says: God will grant his heart success in submitting to His command and being pleased with His decree.
The interpreters said something like what we have said on this.
Mention of those who said that:

c: ʿAlī told me, he said: Abū Ṣāliḥ told us, he said: Muʿāwiya related to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās
m: And whoever believes in God — He will guide his heart
. He means: He will guide his heart to certainty, so that he knows that what befell him was not going to miss him, and what missed him was not going to befall him

c: Naṣr b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Washshāʾ al-Awdī told me, he said: Aḥmad b. Bashīr told us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Ẓabyān, he said:
m: We were with ʿAlqama, and this verse was recited in his presence:
And whoever believes in God — He will guide his heart
. He was asked about it, and he said: He is the man who is struck by a disaster and knows that it is from God, so he submits to it

c: ʿĪsā b. ʿUthmān al-Ramlī told me, he said: Yaḥyā b. ʿĪsā told us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Ẓabyān, he said:
m: I was with ʿAlqama as he was reviewing the codices, and he came to this verse:
No disaster strikes except by permission of God. And whoever believes in God — He will guide his heart
. He said: He is the man. Then he mentioned the like.

c: Ibn Bashshār told us, he said: Abū ʿĀmir told us, he said: Sufyān told us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Ẓabyān, from ʿAlqama
m: No disaster strikes except by permission of God. And whoever believes in God — He will guide his heart
. He said: He is the man who is struck by a disaster and knows that it is from God, so he submits to it and is content

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Mahdī related to me, from al-Thawrī, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Ẓabyān, from ʿAlqama,
m: the like of it, except that he said in his report: so he knows that it is from God's decree, and is content with it and submits.

evidence.text: Naṣr b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Washshāʾ al-Awdī told me, he said: Aḥmad b. Bashīr told us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Ẓabyān, he said: We were with ʿAlqama, and this verse was recited in his presence: {And whoever believes in God — He will guide his heart}.

x: His saying:
h
and God is Knowing of all things
. He says: God has knowledge of everything, of what has been and what will be, and of what is to be before it comes to be.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h

And obey God and obey the Messenger; but if you turn away, then upon Our Messenger is only [the duty of] clear notification (12) God — there is no deity except Him; and upon God let the believers rely (13)
The Exalted says:
h
And obey God
, O people, in His command and His prohibition,
h
and obey the Messenger
, may God bless him and grant him peace,
h
but if you turn away
: if you turn your backs on obedience to God and obedience to His Messenger, being arrogant toward them, and so do not obey God or His Messenger, then
h
upon Our Messenger
Muḥammad is only
h
clear notification

: that he has conveyed to you what I sent him with. Mighty is His praise says: He has excused Himself to you through the conveying, and God is the master of vengeance upon whoever disobeys Him, opposes His command and turns away from Him.
h
God — there is no deity except Him
. Mighty is His praise says: the One you worship, O people, is one God; worship is fit for none other, and you have no deity besides Him,
h
and upon God let the believers rely
. The Exalted says: and upon God, O people, let those who affirm His oneness rely.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h

O you who have believed, indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them. But if you pardon and overlook and forgive — then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful (14)
The Exalted says: O you who have believed God and His Messenger,
h
indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you
who turn you away from the path of God and hold you back from obedience to God,
h
so beware of them

lest you accept from them what they command you of abandoning obedience to God. It is mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning a people who wanted Islam and emigration, but their spouses and children held them back from that.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Yaḥyā b. Ādam and ʿUbayd Allāh b. Mūsā told us, from Isrāʾīl, from Simāk, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said:
m: A man asked him about this verse:
indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them

. He said: These were men who accepted Islam and wanted to come to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, but their spouses and children refused to let them come to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. When they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and saw that the people had gained understanding in the religion, they resolved to punish them; so God, Mighty is His praise, revealed:
O you who have believed, indeed, among your spouses and your children

c: Hannād b. al-Sarī told us, he said: Abū l-Aḥwaṣ told us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrima
m: O you who have believed, indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them

. He said: A man would want to go to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his family would say to him: Where are you going, leaving us? He said: And when he accepted Islam and gained understanding, he said: I will certainly return to those who used to forbid this matter, and I will certainly do such-and-such to them. So God, Mighty is His praise, revealed:
But if you pardon and overlook and forgive — then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful

c: Muḥammad b. Saʿd told me, he said: My father related to me, he said: My uncle related to me, he said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās
m: O you who have believed, indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them

: When a man wanted to emigrate from Mecca to Medina, his wife and child would prevent him, and spared no effort to hold him back from that; so God said: They are enemies to you, so beware of them, and listen and obey, and go on about your business. After that, when a man had been prevented and held back, he would pass by his family and swear — and the oath is a vow — that he would do such-and-such and would punish his family for that; so God, Mighty is His praise, said:
But if you pardon and overlook and forgive — then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Salama told us, he said: Muḥammad b. Isḥāq related to me, from some of his companions, from ʿAṭāʾ b.
m: Yasār, he said: The whole of sura "al-Taghābun" was revealed in Mecca, except these verses:
O you who have believed, indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them

. It was revealed concerning ʿAwf b. Mālik al-Ashjaʿī, who had a family and children; when he wanted to go out on a raid, they would weep to him and soften him, saying: To whom are you leaving us? And he would soften and stay. So there was revealed:
O you who have believed, indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them
; the entire verse in Medina concerning ʿAwf b. Mālik, and the remaining verses to the end of the sura in Medina

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us; and al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Waraqāʾ told us,
m: both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid regarding His saying:
indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them
. He said: The two of them lead him to cut off his kin and to disobey his Lord, and with his love for them he cannot but cut it off

c: Al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said:
m: told us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, the like of it, except that he said: and with his love for them he cannot but obey them (1).

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda
m: O you who have believed, indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them
— the verse. He said: Among them are those who do not enjoin obedience to God and do not forbid disobedience to Him, and they used to hold people back
from emigrating to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and from fighting.

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda
m: indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them
. He said: They forbid Islam and hold people back (3) from it, and they are among the disbelievers, so beware of them

x: I was told, from al-Ḥusayn, he said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say:

c: ʿUbayd told us, he said:
m: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say regarding His saying:
O you who have believed, indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you

— the verse. He said: This is about people of the Arab tribes: a man or a group from a clan would accept Islam and leave their kin, leaving behind their spouses, children and fathers, making for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace; and their kin, spouses, children and fathers would stand up and adjure them by God not to leave them and not to prefer others over them; some of them would soften and return to them, and some would go on until they joined the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: ʿUthmān b. Nājiya and Zayd b. Ḥubāb told us, both said: Yaḥyā b. Wāḍiḥ told us,
m: all from al-Ḥusayn b. Wāqid, he said: ʿAbd Allāh b. Buraydah related to me, from his father, he said: I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, delivering a sermon, when al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn, may God be pleased with them both, came, wearing two red shirts, stumbling and getting up. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came down, took them, lifted them and placed them in his lap, then said: "God and His Messenger have spoken the truth: your wealth and your children are only a trial. I saw these two and could not be patient." Then he went on with his sermon. The wording is that of Abū Kurayb, from Zayd

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you
. He said: He says: enemies to you in your religion, so beware of them for the sake of your religion

x: Muḥammad b. ʿUmar
n
b. ʿAlī al-Muqaddamī told me, he said:

c: Ashʿath b. ʿAbd Allāh told us, he said: Shuʿba told us, from Ismāʿīl b.
m: indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them
. He said: A man would accept Islam, and his family and sons would blame him; so there was revealed:
indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you

x: His saying:
h
But if you pardon and overlook
. He says: if you pardon, O believers, what has passed on their part of turning you away from Islam and emigration, and overlook punishing them for that, and forgive them other sins besides,
h
then indeed, God is Forgiving
to you and to whoever
n
among His servants repents of your sins,
h
Merciful
to you, not punishing you for them after your repentance from them.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h

Your wealth and your children are but a trial, and God has with Him a great reward (15) So fear God as much as you are able and listen and obey and spend; it is better for your selves. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul — it is those who will be the successful (16)
The Exalted says: your wealth, O people, and your children are only a trial, meaning: a test for you in this world.
The interpreters said something like what we have said on this.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda
m: Your wealth and your children are but a trial

x: His saying:
h
and God has with Him a great reward

. He says: and God has with Him a reward for you that is great, if you oppose your children and spouses in obeying God your Lord, and so obey God, Mighty and Majestic, and pay God's due from your wealth. The great reward that is with God: Paradise.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda:
m: and God has with Him a great reward

x: His saying:
h
So fear God as much as you are able

. The Exalted says: so be wary of God, O believers, fear His punishment and guard yourselves from His torment, by performing His obligations, avoiding disobedience to Him, and doing what brings you near to Him, as far as you are able and your capacity reaches. It is mentioned that His saying:
h
So fear God as much as you are able
was revealed after His saying:
h
Fear God as He should be feared
[Āl ʿImrān: 102], as a lightening for the Muslims, and that His saying:
h
So fear God as much as you are able
abrogates His saying:
h
Fear God as He should be feared
Mention of those who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda
m: So fear God as much as you are able and listen and obey
: This is a concession from God, and God is merciful to His servants. God, Mighty is His praise, had sent down before that:
Fear God as He should be feared
. And to fear Him as He should be feared is that He be obeyed and not disobeyed. Then God, Exalted is His mention, lightened it for His servants, and sent down the concession after that, saying:
So fear God as much as you are able and listen and obey
in what you are able, O son of Adam; on this the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took the pledge of allegiance, to listen and obey in what you are able (1).

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda
m: Fear God as He should be feared
So fear God as much as you are able
. We have already given our explanation of the meaning of the abrogating and the abrogated, enough that it need not be repeated in this place
. There is no clear indication in His saying
So fear God as much as you are able
Fear God as He should be feared
Fear God as He should be feared
can carry the sense: fear God as He should be feared in what you are able, [and it has not been established that it has an abrogator]
from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. If that is so, then it is obligatory to apply both of them according to the valid senses they allow.

x: His saying:
h
and listen and obey
. He says: and listen to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and obey him in what he has commanded you and forbidden you,
h
and spend; it is better for your selves
. He says: and spend some of your wealth for your own selves, so that you rescue them from God's punishment. Khayr ("good") in this place is wealth.
His saying:
h
And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul — it is those who will be the successful
. The Exalted says: whoever God protects from the stinginess of his soul, and that is following its desire in what God has forbidden.
Mention of those who said that:

c: ʿAlī told me, he said: Abū Ṣāliḥ told us, he said: Abū Muʿāwiya related to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās
m: And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul
. He says: the desire of his soul, where he follows his desire and does not accept faith.

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from Jāmiʿ b.
m: Shaddād, from al-Aswad b. Hilāl, from Ibn Masʿūd:
And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul
. He said: That he set out for the property of another and eat it

x: His saying:
h
it is those who will be the successful
. He says: so these, who have been protected from the stinginess of their souls, are the prosperous, who have attained their wishes with their Lord.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h
If you loan God a good loan, He will multiply it for you and forgive you; and God is Appreciative and Forbearing (17) Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Exalted in Might, the Wise (18)

The Exalted says: if you spend in the way of God and spend well in it, and seek with your spending reward and recompense, your Lord will multiply that for you, and give you in place of the one seven hundredfold, up to more than that, according to what He wills of multiplication, and will forgive you your sins, pardoning you the punishment for them, along with multiplying your spending that you spend in His way;
h
and God is Appreciative
God is appreciative of those who spend in His way, in the goodness of the recompense He gives them for what they spent in this world in His way,
h
Forbearing
. He says: forbearing toward those who disobey Him, by not hastening their punishment;
h
Knower of the unseen and the witnessed
. He says: Knower of what the eyes of His servants do not see and which is hidden from their sight, and of what they witness and see with their eyes,
h
the Exalted in Might
He means: severe in
n
His vengeance upon whoever disobeys Him and opposes His command and prohibition,
h
the Wise
in His management of His creation and His directing them in what is good for them.
End of the commentary on the sura "al-Taghābun".
